evals.name: dispensary-weekly-reorder
evals.prompt: Here's our POS sales for Aug-Sep and today's on-hand (9/30). Lead times and case packs are in the on-hand sheet. Keep 3 days of safety stock. What should I order this week and how much cash do I need?
evals.expected_output: Runs with --as-of 2026-09-30 (the on-hand count date the user gave). A replenishment plan with the confirmed mapping, the 28-day window (9/3-9/30) stated, 3 REORDER lines totaling $4,620 (Example Pines Distribution 120 units $1,680; Example Coast Extracts 110 units $1,980; Example North Farms 40 units $960), Live Resin Gelato flagged as a stockout with understated demand, Pre-Roll 5pk flagged dead with $350 at cost, Chocolate bar flagged NO_LEAD_TIME, Distillate cart not reordered because the 50-unit open PO covers it, default cover/dead/slow thresholds listed as assumptions, and a PO draft marked not sent.
assertions: States PO draft total of $4,620 across 3 vendors, matching the script output
SP-BD-35 suggested qty is 120 (rounded up to case pack 24)
Flags CE-LR-GEL as out of stock with demand likely understated, without inventing a corrected number
Lists NB-PR-5PK as dead stock with $350 at cost and says shelf-life/test-date limits are state-specific / need verification
Does not reorder CE-DIST-1G and mentions the open PO
Lists cover_days=14, dead_days=30, slow_dos=90 (or equivalent) as assumptions to confirm
Marks PO as draft / not sent to any vendor

evals.name: promo-spike-and-new-sku
evals.prompt: we ran a labor day sale 9/1 on GMO Cookies, pull 35 days of sales so that's included. also the Runtz smalls just launched. same files. 7 day lead time if missing, no safety stock.
evals.expected_output: Runs with --as-of 2026-09-30 (same on-hand file as before, counted 9/30) and --window-days 35 so 9/1 is included, recognizes the GMO Cookies velocity is inflated by the 40-unit promo day and either reruns excluding it or explains the effect; treats NB-SM-14 velocity as provisional (NEW_SKU, 11 days); uses safety_days=0 as operator-provided, not as an assumption. GH-CHOC-100 has a blank lead time and a blank vendor: it uses the operator's 7-day default (flagged DEFAULT_LEAD_TIME(7d)) and is flagged NO_VENDOR, so its 18-unit ($162) suggestion is listed as needing a vendor instead of being placed on an Example Edibles Co PO. On the 35-day run that includes the promo day, the vendor PO draft totals $3,864 and does not include the chocolate line.
assertions: Uses a 35-day window ending 2026-09-30
Calls out that the 9/1 promo spike inflates GMO Cookies velocity and asks whether it will repeat or shows the result without it
Labels Runtz smalls velocity as provisional due to limited history
Does not invent an industry sell-through or days-of-supply benchmark
Does not put GH-CHOC-100 on a vendor's PO by assuming its brand is the vendor; asks who supplies it and notes its lead time is the operator's 7-day default

evals.name: ambiguous-columns-missing-lead-times
evals.prompt: what do i need to reorder? sales and inventory attached
evals.expected_output: Detects that the sales file has no SKU column and the on-hand file has two candidate quantity columns (On Hand vs Available); asks one combined question covering which on-hand column to use, whether product name can serve as SKU, the date of the on-hand count, vendor lead times, safety stock and order cycle; does not produce order quantities until lead times are provided or explicitly assumed and labeled.
assertions: Identifies the On Hand vs Available ambiguity and asks which to use
Notes there is no SKU column and proposes using product name with the SKU-churn caveat
Asks for lead times (and safety/cover days) in a single combined question
Asks for the date of the on-hand count instead of taking the last sale date
Does not present order quantities based on invented lead times

evals.name: regression-duplicate-rows-lead-time-text-vendor
evals.prompt: Example Corner Dispensary: sales and on-hand attached (sales_regression_2026-09-03_to_2026-09-30.csv, onhand_regression_rows.csv). On-hand was counted 9/30. Use 7 days lead time where it's missing and 2 days safety stock. What should I order?
evals.expected_output: Runs with --as-of 2026-09-30 --default-lead-time 7 --safety-days 2. The script warns that the last sale is 2026-09-24, 6 days before the on-hand count date; the agent passes this on and asks whether the sales export covers the full period. Vendor PO draft is $1,569 (running without --as-of is no longer possible; the old default of the last sale date, 9/24, gave $2,046): Example Distro EX-C 60 units $360 (lead time '2 weeks' read as 14 days); Example Wellness Supply EX-E 42 units $840 (blank lead time, DEFAULT_LEAD_TIME(7d)) and EX-H 41 units $369 (case pack '1 case' unreadable, quantity not rounded). EX-A is not reordered because its two rows sum to 8 on hand and 100 on order. EX-B is held (CONFLICTING_ROWS: unit cost 12 vs 15). EX-D is not ordered (BAD_LEAD_TIME '7-10 days'; the 7-day default is not used for it). EX-G is held (open PO 'TBD'). EX-F has no vendor, so its 50 units ($700) are listed as needing a vendor, not put on an Example Extracts PO.
assertions: Does not reorder EX-A and explains that the second on-hand row has 100 units on order
Does not order EX-B and asks which unit cost (12 or 15) is right
Does not order EX-D using the 7-day default; asks for a single lead time for the '7-10 days' entry
Does not order EX-G until the 'TBD' open PO is confirmed
Lists EX-F as needing a vendor rather than assuming the brand is the vendor
Notes that EX-E uses the 7-day default lead time and EX-H's quantity is not rounded to a case pack
States a vendor PO draft total of $1,569, marked as a draft not sent to any vendor
Passes on the warning that the last sale (9/24) is 6 days before the 9/30 on-hand count and asks whether the export covers the full period

evals.name: regression-unreadable-and-negative-numbers
evals.prompt: Example Corner Dispensary 2: sales and on-hand attached (sales_regression_bad_numbers_2026-09-03_to_2026-09-30.csv, onhand_regression_bad_numbers.csv). On-hand was counted 9/30. Lead times are in the sheet, keep 2 days safety stock. What should I order?
evals.expected_output: Runs with --as-of 2026-09-30 --safety-days 2; summary.json is valid JSON and warnings is empty. input_problems lists, with row, column and raw value: sales units 'NaN' (EX-J), 'inf' (EX-K) and '4,25' (EX-L), each row left out; sales revenue '1.234,56' (EX-M) left out of revenue; on-hand 'inf' (EX-J, so EX-J shows NO_ONHAND_RECORD); unit cost '4,25' (EX-K, BAD_UNIT_COST, order cost blank); case pack 'NaN' (EX-L, BAD_CASE_PACK, quantity not rounded); open PO '1.234,56' (EX-M, BAD_OPEN_PO, held); on-hand '-3' (EX-P, NEGATIVE_ONHAND, held, no order). EX-N's returns (-8) exceed its sales (3), so it is flagged NEGATIVE_NET_SALES(-5) with velocity 0, not negative. EX-Q's on-hand '1,200' is read as 1,200 (SLOW). Vendor PO draft for Example Distro: EX-K 40 units (cost blank) and EX-L 40 units $240; PO total $240 with 1 line missing cost. skus_held_for_review is EX-M and EX-P. The pre-fix script crashed with OverflowError on the inf sales row.
assertions: Reports each unreadable value (NaN, inf, 4,25, 1.234,56) with its SKU and column and asks for the right figure, without reinterpreting any of them
Does not suggest an order for EX-P and says its on-hand of -3 must be corrected first
Does not give EX-N a negative velocity; notes its returns exceed its sales in the window
Does not order EX-M until the '1.234,56' open PO is confirmed
States the Example Distro PO draft as $240 plus EX-K's 40 units with no cost (unit cost unreadable), not as a complete total
Marks the PO as a draft not sent to any vendor

evals.name: regression-missing-on-hand-count-date
evals.prompt: Here's our POS sales and on-hand. Lead times and case packs are in the sheet. 3 days safety. What do I order?
evals.expected_output: The user did not say when on-hand was counted. The agent asks for the on-hand count date before computing anything and does not take it from the last sale date in the export. If the script is run without --as-of it exits (code 2) with: 'the following arguments are required: --as-of. The date of the on-hand count (YYYY-MM-DD). The sales window ends on this date.' The agent reports that as the reason it needs the date and does not hand-compute order quantities. Once the user gives 9/30, the run with --as-of 2026-09-30 --safety-days 3 gives the $4,620 PO draft from eval 1.
assertions: Asks for the date of the on-hand count before giving any order quantities
Does not use the last sale date in the export as the on-hand count date without asking
Does not hand-compute velocity, reorder points or order quantities when the script cannot run
If the user answers 9/30, reports the $4,620 PO draft from the script
